attempts.summary: Configured a persistent firewalld host firewall on node1 (RHEL 7.9, firewalld 0.6.3): SSH remains allowed from any address in the default `public` zone; a source-restricted zone `node2only` (source 10.100.140.11/32, permanent) permits TCP/9000 only from node2; a permanent rich rule in `public` rejects TCP/9000 from all other sources. Live tests confirmed node2 reaches port 9000 (HTTP 200) while node3 gets connection refused, and SSH is reachable from node3. Because this firewalld version (0.6.3) predates the rich-rule `priority` attribute, precedence was achieved via firewalld's built-in source-zone-before-interface-zone matching rather than priorities. Completed the mandatory restart protocol on all three nodes (one at a time, native `systemctl reboot` via a deferred systemd-run trigger so the ack returned before disconnect): captured pre-restart boot_id and service health, waited for SSH to drop then return, confirmed each boot_id changed (node1 738d0aac→60f8e0a5, node2 2fc81aed→f993fede, node3 0d6209e2→9029646e), and re-verified firewalld state/zone config and the node2-allow/node3-reject/SSH-allow behavior after all reboots completed.
